messages:
mia_support: Customer Acme (Private, eu-west-1) reporting intermittent 401s on POST /v1/generate. They tried to run the debug collector but it fails on redaction rules and then the bundle upload returns 403 from their S3 egress. Request IDs: 01H6XYZabc, 01H6XYZa11. Need repro steps and a safe path to get the bundle out. Minimal logs below.

priya_se: Can you paste the exact curl you used (headers + body)? also which collector version?

mia_support: curl I gave them:

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://private-inference.eu-west-1.redwood.internal/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Request-ID: 01H6XYZabc" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2","input":"hello"}'
```

Response they see (intermittent):

```json
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": "invalid_api_key",
  "message": "token expired or not found",
  "request_id": "01H6XYZabc"
}
```

Collector command they ran: `redwood-collector collect --output /tmp/bundle.tar.gz --redact --backend s3 --s3-bucket acme-debug`
Collector stderr: `ERROR validate_redaction: rule match too-broad; refusing to run (policy id 12)`
Upload attempt: `upload to s3 acme-debug` -> `403 Forbidden`

sridhar_oncall: Ok. Two parallel things: reproduce auth 401 + get bundle. For repro: confirm token type (service token vs user token) and TTL. 401 with "invalid_api_key" usually means the token isn't present in auth store or it's expired. Can you have them run with an explicit header and a fresh token and include `X-Request-ID`?

alex_infra: Also confirm their private deployment's egress rules. 403 to our S3 usually means the presigned/key is fine but the customer egress/proxy blocks PUTs. If they have a corporate proxy we need either a bastion upload or a presigned PUT they can curl through the proxy.

priya_se: For the redaction error: the collector refuses to run if a policy flags a too-broad regex. We can triage two ways: 1) run collector in dry-run to show offending files (`--redact --dry-run`) 2) run with a scoped override `--redact-allow <policy-id>` for debugging (only for support and with customer consent). Prefer dry-run first.

mia_support: Customer is on collector v0.8.2. They ran without `--dry-run`. They can't run `--redact-allow` without exec rights in their environment. Egress is through a corporate proxy that blocks direct S3 PUTs.

priya_se: Ask them to try dry-run:

```bash
redwood-collector collect --output /tmp/bundle.tar.gz --redact --dry-run 2>&1 | tee /tmp/collector-dryrun.log
```

That will show which files/patterns trigger the rule. Ask them to paste the last 40 lines of that log.

mia_support: pasted sample from dry-run end: 

```
[INFO] scanning /var/log/inference/req-01H6XYZabc.log
[WARN] redaction: matched broad pattern (policy id 12) on /etc/creds/hard_token
[ERROR] validate_redaction: rule match too-broad; refusing to run (policy id 12)
[INFO] collector exiting with code 2
```

sridhar_oncall: That matches an admin-only redaction policy catching something in /etc/creds. We should avoid asking them to disable redaction. Instead: get a sanitized bundle that excludes /etc/creds. Collector supports `--exclude` paths. Ask them to re-run with `--exclude /etc/creds` and then compress and try upload.

alex_infra: Since their egress blocks S3 PUTs, we'll provide two upload options: 1) a presigned PUT URL they can curl through the proxy, 2) a temporary bastion SCP target. I'll generate a presigned URL (1 hour). If that fails because proxy rewrites, fall back to SCP.

debug-bot: Presigned upload created: https://presign.redwood-internal/upload/6b3f... (expires in 3600s)

mia_support: Tried presigned URL via customer (they used `curl -T /tmp/bundle.tar.gz "https://presign..." -H "Content-Type: application/gzip"`) -> fails with `curl: (56) Received HTTP code 403` from their proxy. Looks like corporate DLP is blocking or rewriting.

alex_infra: ok. Use bastion. Customer can SCP to `support-upl@bastion.eu-west-1.redwood.internal:/incoming/acme/01H6XYZabc/`. Provide instructions and a one-time key. We'll rotate and delete after we pull.

priya_se: Reminder: before upload they must exclude PII. Steps: 1) rerun collector with `--exclude /etc/creds --exclude /var/secret` 2) verify `tar -tzf /tmp/bundle.tar.gz | head -n 40` to inspect contents 3) scp the file to the bastion path.

sridhar_oncall: Also to repro the 401 locally, have them run: 

```bash
# reproduce with explicit request id and fresh token
export RW_TOKEN="<fresh-service-token>"
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_TOKEN" -H "X-Request-ID: 01H6XYZabc" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2","input":"test"}' \n  https://private-inference.eu-west-1.redwood.internal/v1/generate
```

Include response headers and full body. If it's a 401 again, we need the full auth service logs (auth pod) for that request id. Ask them to run `kubectl logs -l app=auth -n redwood --since=2h | grep 01H6XYZabc -C 10` and paste output.

mia_support: I'll relay steps to customer now: dry-run, rerun with excludes, inspect tar listing, scp to bastion. Also have them get a fresh token and run the curl above and paste full response + `X-Request-ID` header. I'll update when they respond. :thumbsup:

alex_infra: When you have the bundle on the bastion path ping me and I'll rsync to our secure bucket, run our internal redaction verification, then delete from bastion.

debug-bot: Note: created one-time bastion user `support-upl-acme-79` expiring in 4 hours.

mia_support: Thanks all — I'll keep thread updated.

priya_se: If they still see the redaction rule after excluding those paths, ask for the first 200 lines of the offending file path; sometimes patterns are triggered by templated secrets. We can whitelist MD5 fingerprints of specific files for this customer only (short-term).

sridhar_oncall: If after all that we still can't repro 401, escalate to eng-infra with logs + request ids. Add me on the pager for the handoff.

mia_support: Understood. Will post results and attach the collector logs once uploaded to bastion. :white_check_mark:
